_comment: Gate calibration controls (S0). The gate decides which rope configurations
may run, so an uncalibrated gate converts 'we did not check' into 'we
checked and it passed'.
EVERY control is judged against a DECLARED native baseline at its OWN
context and model. A control with no baseline at its own context reports
'no baseline' and is NOT measured -- and an unmeasured control is neither a
pass nor a detected failure. The earlier file flagged only P3 as a
baseline, so P1/P2 (and the Llama-2 negative) were unmeasured and their
verdicts were meaningless.
The baselines are separate rows on the SAME seed as the control they
score. The seed selects the document, the offset and the continuation, so
the same seed makes the ratio a PAIRED contrast: the only thing that
differs between a control and its baseline is the rope configuration,
which is what the gate is testing. A baseline on a different seed would
fold sampling variation into the ratio -- a difference between two
samples, not between two configurations. (These references used seed 7
against candidates on seed 42 until the pairing check in the 2026-10-06
revision caught it.) The baseline is still a SEPARATE row with the native
rope, never the control itself, so the ratio is not 1.0 by construction
The tolerance is FIXED at 1.5x by the 2026-10-06 plan revision, so these
controls no longer set it. Their role is now a falsification test of the
gate at that fixed tolerance: positives must pass, negatives must fail.
The positives' measured ratios are also the evidence that the gate's
perplexity measurement is stable well inside 1.5x -- if a positive ratio
ever approached 1.5, the tolerance would not have margin.
The two negatives are not hypothetical: 'arm4_f2_construction' is the rope
dict that replaced Llama-3.1-8B's shipped llama3 block in the ARM4 f2 cell,
where the target emitted EOS at token 0 and the acceptance collapse was
published as a result. 'llama2_misanchored' is YaRN anchored on the context
length instead of the 4096 base, which measured 57x native perplexity
expect: 'pass' | 'fail' is the REQUIRED verdict. A control that disagrees
means the gate is wrong, not the control.

candidates.name: P2_declared_shipped_64k
candidates._what_it_is: The 64k rung's positive control: Llama-3.1-8B at 64k with its SHIPPED llama3 block declared explicitly (factor 8, anchor 8192) instead of left implicit as rope_type 'none'. It is judged against B_native_64k on the same (context, model, seed), so the two score the same window and the ratio is a paired contrast. The expected verdict is PASS and it is known rather than hoped: _build_hf_config reproduces the shipped rope_scaling dict bit-for-bit from these three parameters (verified offline: identical dict, identical inv_freq, max abs diff 0.0), so the model's numerics are identical to the baseline's by construction.
candidates._what_it_replaces: P2_native_64k, which was byte-identical to B_native_64k (same model, rope, context, seed and revision) and therefore scored a second measurement of itself: two rows reported one measurement, and both were reported as failures. A native candidate at its baseline's own (context, model, seed) has no same-sample reference other than itself, so no seed or window change can remove that duplication without leaving the candidate unpaired; the duplication is structural, not accidental. Declaring the rope removes it, because the candidate and the reference are then different configurations.
candidates._what_it_tests: The rope DECLARATION path -- the path the ARM4 f2 defect lived in, where a config dict replaced the shipped llama3 block. Today that path is exercised only by negative controls, i.e. only in the direction of expecting it to fail; this control exercises it in the direction of expecting it to reproduce the shipped rope, and it fails loudly (rope mismatch, or a ppl ratio away from 1.0) if the declaration path ever stops being a no-op.

candidates._what_it_reproduces: The historical bug: no anchor override, so transformers 4.47.1 routes the YaRN band onto config.max_position_embeddings = the context length. This is the construction that measured 826.9 perplexity at 32k vs 14.45 correctly anchored.
